question: Which Five-Year Plan was interrupted due to the Indo-Pak War and economic crisis?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Third Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Third Five-Year Plan (1961-1966) aimed to achieve self-reliance in food production and industrial growth in India.
 
• This plan was interrupted due to the **Indo-China War of 1962** and the **Indo-Pak War of 1965**, causing economic turmoil.
 
• The government shifted focus from planned economic development to **defense and emergency management**.
 
• Severe droughts in 1965-1966 also further disrupted the objectives of the plan, leading to a crisis in agricultural production.
 
• The economic challenges during this period necessitated a deviation from the planned targets and resulted in the introduction of annual plans or "Plan Holidays" from 1966 to 1969.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans in India**

 
 
• India's Five-Year Plans were a series of centralized economic and social development strategies implemented from 1951 to 2017.
 
• The Planning Commission was responsible for formulating these plans until its replacement by the NITI Aayog in 2015.
 
• The plans aimed to boost economic growth, improve the standard of living, and address social inequalities.
 
 
 
• **Plan Holidays (1966-1969)**
 
 
• Plan Holidays were introduced after the Third Five-Year Plan due to financial constraints caused by wars and droughts.
 
• During this period, the government adopted annual plans to address short-term goals and stabilize the economy.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Indo-Pak War on Economy**
 
 
• The 1965 Indo-Pak War strained India's financial resources, diverting funds from developmental activities to defense expenditures.
 
• It disrupted trade and led to inflation, further complicating economic recovery efforts.
 
 
 
• **Green Revolution**
 
 
• The Green Revolution, initiated in the late 1960s, was a response to the agricultural crisis during the Third Plan era.
 
• It focused on high-yield crop varieties, modern irrigation techniques, and the use of fertilizers to increase agricultural productivity.
